subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bold part of the sentence.

The price of petrol **has increased yesterday.**
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**has increased yesterday**" is incorrect because the present perfect tense ("has increased") cannot be used with a specific time reference like "yesterday."
 
• Instead, the simple past tense ("**rose yesterday**" or "**increased yesterday**") is appropriate when referring to a specific event that occurred in the past.
 
• Option 2, "**increased yesterday**," is the most grammatically correct and concise choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The price of petrol increased yesterday."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "rose yesterday" is grammatically correct but may not be the best choice depending on the context. "Rose" is less commonly used in this particular sentence.
 
• **Option 3:** "has been increased yesterday" is incorrect because the present perfect tense ("has been increased") cannot be paired with "yesterday," which is a specific past time.
 
• **Option 4:** "risen yesterday" is incorrect because "risen" requires an auxiliary verb to form a proper sentence (e.g., "has risen yesterday").
